name: SpaceX Starmind AI1 orbital data center satellite
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'SpaceX AI Satellites' type (Starmind AI1, a million-satellite dawn-dusk disk). Body frame: +Z to the Sun, +X toward nadir. Two sun-pointing wings spanning 70 m; edge-on radiators zenith and nadir of the bus, 20 m top to bottom. Widths derived from the 250 kW design power. Kept small (10 lobes) because a million satellites fly it.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: Sun-pointing panels (+Z to the Sun), +X toward nadir; panels tilted off the Sun by the flare-mitigation slider
sources.source: Starmind AI1 as specified by the project owner (2026-09-24): 'two large sun pointing panels with a wingspan of 70m', 'edge on radiators on the top and bottom of the bus with a deployed height of 20m'. Press (The Robotics Media / Winzheng, 2026-08): 'about 30 meters tall when deployed, with a wingspan of roughly 75 meters', '75-meter solar panels, 30-meter radiative cooling panels, and peak computing power of 250 kilowatts'; SatNews 2026-09-19 (FCC debris analysis): 'up to 4,000 kilograms' per node. The tilt joint is the v1.1 legacy type's (SunTrackingTilted), kept for the slider.

sources.value: two 32.5 x 9.2 m rigid glass-covered wings, 70 m tip to tip (598 m2)
sources.source: Starmind AI1 as specified by the project owner (2026-09-24): 'two large sun pointing panels with a wingspan of 70m', 'edge on radiators on the top and bottom of the bus with a deployed height of 20m'. Press (The Robotics Media / Winzheng, 2026-08): 'about 30 meters tall when deployed, with a wingspan of roughly 75 meters', '75-meter solar panels, 30-meter radiative cooling panels, and peak computing power of 250 kilowatts'; SatNews 2026-09-19 (FCC debris analysis): 'up to 4,000 kilograms' per node. Span sourced; width DERIVED: 250 kW at ~30% cell efficiency and 1361 W/m2 needs ~610 m2, which also matches the legacy type's 600 m2.
